transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-18 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~50 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Eliot Park (Redwood SE), Jordan Reyes (Redwood SE); Ana Morales (Veritas Head of Platform), Priyank Shah (Veritas SRE), Liam O'Connor (Veritas Security), Sofia Ramos (Veritas PM)

Summary:
Quick integration-focused discovery about Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private for large-scale financial workloads. Key topics: SDKs and LangChain/LlamaIndex support, gateway/proxy architecture, rate limits & quotas, observability hooks, security/KMS and compliance. Customer wants predictable latency, strict auditability, and an integration pattern that fits their platform and LangChain-based agents.

Topics:
- SDK support (python/node/go) and example connectors
- LangChain and LlamaIndex integration patterns
- Gateway/proxy sidecar approach and request routing
- Rate limiting, quotas, and burst behavior for peak trading hours
- Observability hooks: traces, per-route metrics, token-level cost breakdown
- Private deployment options (VPC, on-prem) and KMS/HSM integration

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intros — I'm Maya, AE — Eliot and Jordan from our SE team are here for the technical bits.
[00:18] Ana (Veritas): Hi, Ana here, head of platform. we run most AI routing through an internal gateway. looking at options for hosted vs dedicated because of cost and latency.
[00:34] Eliot (Redwood): Great. can you talk to current stack? we heard you're using LangChain and LlamaIndex for a lot of your agent workflows.
[00:46] Priyank (Veritas): yeah we have several Lang Chain pipelines, mostly python, some node. we also use an in-house proxy for rate limiting. volume is spiky — batch payroll and trading windows at 9:30 and 16:00, so short bursts that are high qps.
[01:05] Jordan (Redwood): Got it. do you run any on-prem inference today or is it all cloud?
[01:12] Ana: 90% cloud; security wants VPC-private options for anything with PII. also, our security team will want audit logs and KMS support.
[01:22] Maya: That's expected for finance. quick high level: Redwood Hosted gives fastest path, Dedicated is reserved GPU capacity for predictable throughput, and Private gives VPC or on-prem control. All have the same API surface.
[01:39] Liam (Veritas): On the security front — SOC2, encryption at rest/in-transit, and HSM/KMS are musts. Also, we need proof that audit logs can be exported to our SIEM.
[01:53] Eliot: We have SOC2 docs and KMS integrations; we can export audit logs and forward to SIEMs. i'll attach the security pack after.

[05:01] Ana: Integration specifics: our platform uses a gateway that proxies to backends. whats the recommended pattern for Redwood calls — direct SDK calls from services, or proxy everything through our gateway?
[05:23] Jordan: Good question. two common patterns: 1) direct SDK calls from app services with token-based auth, good for latency; 2) route through your gateway as a single integration point for observability and control. we also support a hybrid — SDK in services with request routing rules at the gateway for certain endpoints.
[05:45] Priyank: If we go direct, how do we handle rate limits/quota enforcement? we already have quotas per-tenant.
[05:55] Eliot: Redwood exposes per-key rate limits and per-route quotas; you can also set throttles in Dedicated. we can map your tenant id to Redwood API keys and enforce quotas client-side and server-side. there's also webhooks for limit events.

[09:30] Sofia: For LangChain/LlamaIndex — are there official connectors or examples? our ML team is nervous about compatibility.
[09:42] Jordan: Yes, we maintain official SDKs and example connectors for Lang Chain and LlamaIndex. we have a small demo repo that shows streaming responses, function calls, and how to inject prompts via LlamaIndex. we'll share code snippets that plug into your existing Lang Chain agents.
[10:10] Ana: Streaming is important — for agent UX. what about prefix/KV cache? we use lots of short, contextual queries that would benefit.
[10:22] Eliot: Redwood offers prefix caching and KV cache patterns in the runtime. on Dedicated, you can keep hot KV in memory per-pool to reduce token costs and latency. for hosted, we have managed caching with configurable TTLs; we can expose hooks to invalidate cache via the API.

[14:05] Priyank: About gateway/proxy — we prefer a sidecar pattern if performance isn't impacted. can Redwood run behind a local gateway that proxies to Redwood endpoints without breaking streaming or function calls?
[14:22] Jordan: Yes. many customers run a gateway or sidecar. important points: keep websocket/stream connections alive and map streaming endpoints correctly. also preserve client IPs if you need per-user routing. we have docs showing a sample nginx/envoy config and a small node proxy example.
[14:45] Liam: Any gotchas with latency when using a proxy? we need 95th percentile under 120ms on small prompts during trading hours.
[14:55] Eliot: Proxy adds RTT, but with good placement (same region, private peering), the overhead is typically 10-30ms. Dedicated gives you predictable queueing — we can model your bursts to size pools to keep 95th below 120ms.

[20:00] Ana: How do you handle authentication and API key rotation, especially if we map one key per-tenant?
[20:12] Maya: We support per-key usage metrics, SSO for console, and automated key rotation via API. for Dedicated/Private you can integrate with your KMS/HSM for signing.

[24:40] Priyank: Observability hooks — we want traces, per-route token breakdowns, and cost attribution for teams. is that built in?
[24:52] Jordan: Yes. Redwood Console provides per-route and per-model dashboards, token-level cost, and tracing hooks you can forward to your tracing backend (we have exporters for Jaeger/Datadog). there are also tracing headers you can pass to correlate requests end-to-end.
[25:20] Ana: Will those traces include model version and quantization profile? we test different quant modes for cost/quality trade-offs.
[25:33] Eliot: We record model variant and quantization metadata per request in the traces and logs. you can also tag rollouts and compare quality metrics across prompt sets in Redwood Optimize.

[28:00] Sofia: On the POC — what's the fastest way to validate latency & cost?
[28:12] Jordan: Two options: 1) give you hosted tokens to run a quick benchmark against our managed clusters; or 2) provision a short-term Dedicated pool with reserved capacity to mimic production. for realistic numbers, Dedicated POC is better because it isolates noisy neighbors.
[28:36] Priyank: We'd like to run both — hosted for quick functional checks and a Dedicated POC for latency/cost.

[33:10] Liam: Legal/procurement will ask about data residency and contract terms; can Redwood support EU-only regions and customer-managed logging retention?
[33:24] Maya: Yes, EU regions available; retention is configurable for enterprise tiers and Private. we'll include standard contract language and a note about on-prem options.

[37:00] Ana: A couple product nitty-gritty: do you support long context windows and what's the max seq length we should expect?
[37:12] Eliot: Depends on model; we support up to 128k with special kernels on certain model variants. default high-capacity configs are 16k-32k. we'll provide recommended kernel/model combos for your workload.

[41:40] Sofia: Any limitations integrating with LlamaIndex that we should watch for? embeddings, chunking, metadata?
[41:52] Jordan: Llama Index workflows work fine; watch out for embedding costs at scale. we support batching embeddings and caching to reduce costs, and provide hooks to surface chunking fingerprints to help dedupe.

[45:10] Maya: Recap and next steps: we'll send SOC2/security pack, share LangChain/LlamaIndex examples and a sample proxy config, provision a trial account and prepare Dedicated POC sizing based on the traffic profile Priyank will send. schedule technical deep-dive for 2027-08-24.
[45:40] Ana: That sounds good. thanks everyone.
[45:46] Priyank: I'll send traffic histograms and 95/99 latency targets by Monday.
[46:00] Liam: i'll follow up on encryption/KMS details.
[46:10] Maya: Great. we'll follow up with the materials and calendar invite.

End of meeting.
